sampling_model.design: One binary treatment path is drawn from a chosen \(D\in\mathfrak D_T\); the assignment is the only randomness.
sampling_model.units: A single fixed experimental unit observed at \(T\) ordered periods.
sampling_model.treatment: \(X_t\in\{-1,+1\}\), with random treatment counts and zero prehistory.
sampling_model.overlap: Global sign symmetry and exact pairwise orthogonality replace independent assignment; no fixed-count constraint is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The fixed vectors \(g\) and \(e\) range jointly over \(\mathcal H_T\); no nuisance law, plug-in variance, or Wald approximation is used.

body.tldr: For a single fixed impulse-response path, all balanced pairwise-orthogonal binary designs have identical first and second moments but can have different fourth-order risk for the displayed unbiased moment estimator. Global sign symmetry is not imposed: averaging any legal law with its global-sign reflection preserves the diagonal risk blocks, removes the signal--disturbance cross block, and weakly improves risk. Over this maximal class the project derives the exact all-horizon minimax MSE and complete optimizer face for \(K=2\), including the necessary zero-cross-vector condition, the even--odd parity gap, mirrored-edge-sign attaining laws, the exact iid threshold, and the legal intersection with stationary homogeneous random-switch laws. It also constructs a balanced stationary finite-state randomized Golay-block law and proves that, for fixed \(K,q\), it attains the spectral disturbance floor shared by the finite-horizon and stationary limits.

project_justification.gap: Existing N-of-1 inference fixes independent toggling, while current temporal optimal-design theory restricts assignment to structured Markov families and an ordinary-least-squares criterion, and recent network-design work relaxes an explicit fourth-order Rademacher objective to Gaussian covariance optimization. None optimizes the realizable fourth moments over all balanced pairwise-orthogonal one-path laws under a joint coefficient--disturbance ellipsoid, nor handles the signal--disturbance cross block of an unsymmetrized law.
project_justification.niche: The niche is global optimal randomization for an already-identified causal moment under fixed potential outcomes, with the balanced pairwise-orthogonal assignment law as the design variable. Global sign symmetry is only a provably without-loss representative, and the deliverable remains exact minimax risk for the displayed estimator rather than all-estimator optimality.
project_justification.fill: The block-risk lemma proves the symmetrization reduction, the parity theorem solves the first nontrivial finite problem and its full optimizer face, the iid corollary supplies the exact threshold, and the class-separation theorem isolates iid as the sole legal stationary homogeneous random-switch law. The Golay-block theorem supplies a finite-state balanced stationary optimizer, a fourth-moment tensor certificate, and the spectral lower bound establishing global asymptotic optimality over the enlarged finite and stationary classes.

body.related_work: Liang and Recht (2025), Section 2.2, equation (6), the immediately following quadratic-chaos display, Appendix A.1, and Section 6 define the same linear causal estimands and moment estimator and analyze it under independent Rademacher toggling. Their iid law is a strict subclass of the balanced pairwise-orthogonal laws optimized here, and the joint coefficient--disturbance ellipsoid extends the fixed-path comparison; global sign symmetry is not a substantive restriction because the present block-matrix argument proves sign averaging weakly improves risk. Guo and Liang (2026), Definition 3.6, define an asymptotic ordinary-least-squares objective; Definition 4.1 defines stationary homogeneous random-switch designs; and Theorem 4.6 sends robust-design minimizers to \((1/2,1/2)\). Their full random-switch class is generally outside the legal balanced pairwise-orthogonal class. The transferable comparison is exactly the intersection theorem: balance gives equal transition probabilities and lag-one orthogonality then leaves iid alone. The finite iid-threshold result concerns fixed-path worst-case MSE of the displayed moment estimator, so it does not identify their ordinary-least-squares criterion with this one. Thiyageswaran et al. (2026), arXiv:2601.17145v1, Appendix F.3, pp. 31--32, derive a fourth-order Rademacher objective in Example 10 and then use a Gaussian covariance relaxation. That establishes the relevance of fourth moments but neither characterizes realizable binary temporal laws nor supplies the zero-prehistory parity and stationary certificates proved here. Bojinov, Simchi-Levi, and Zhao (2023) study regular-switchback minimax design under a different bounded-carryover adversary. Golay (1961), Davis and Jedwab (1999), Tellambura, Guo, and Barton (1998), and Mazáč (2024) provide complementary-sequence and Rudin--Shapiro ingredients; they do not establish the one-path design-based minimax result. Bandeira and Kunisky (2018) and Manchester (2010) concern relaxations rather than the exact realizable causal design class.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The required early audits passed: exact enumeration at \(T=5\) reproduces the parity certificate and its equality set, and the \(L=8,16\) affine Golay blocks for \(K=3,4\) give boundary covariance \(H_d\), zero internal--boundary covariance, and the two-block identity \(2M_L+H_d\). These computations are audits rather than proof premises. The parity result is proved by pointwise integer certificates, while the stationary result uses the established random-phase endpoint tensor, zero-prehistory remainder, and finite-state construction. The joint ellipsoid still permits a disturbance spike for which \(\sqrt T(\widehat\tau-\tau)\) is two-point, so no uniform Wald conclusion is claimed.
body.honest_scope: The theorems optimize the fixed-path worst-case mean squared error of the displayed unbiased moment estimator, not risk over all estimators. The legal class consists of balanced pairwise-orthogonal binary laws; global sign symmetry is only a without-loss representative obtained by mixing a law with its sign reflection. Treatment counts remain random: exact fixed balance is incompatible with pairwise orthogonality because it would force both \(\mathbb E(\sum_tX_t)^2=0\) and \(\mathbb E(\sum_tX_t)^2=T\). The result is binary and does not cover a third arm or general multi-arm designs. The full Guo--Liang random-switch class is generally outside the legal class, so only its iid intersection is compared, and no numerical equality with their asymptotic ordinary-least-squares criterion is asserted. Gaussian or covariance relaxations do not certify binary temporal moment-body membership. Under iid assignment and \(K=2\), \(\mathbb E S_T^2=T-1\); the mirrored law instead attains \(a_T\). The exact general finite-\(K\) realizable lag-four body and an explicit uniform \(T^{-1}\) boundary rate remain open.
